1.explanation: Each of these files defines a component that currently declares an ariaLabel prop in its propTypes (or TypeScript interface) and applies it to an element’s aria‐label attribute.  According to React’s accessibility guidelines, all aria-* attributes should be kebab‐case, so we must update these components to accept ['aria-label'] instead of ariaLabel, deprecate the old camelCased prop, update prop‐type definitions and TypeScript interfaces, and adjust the rendering logic to prefer the new prop name while maintaining backward compatibility during a deprecation period.
1.bug_scenario: The issue is an inconsistency in how accessibility labels are exposed across our React components. In React’s JSX all aria-* attributes must use hyphen-case (e.g. aria-label), yet many Carbon components currently only accept a camelCased ariaLabel prop.  In the Storybook for Modal (v1.17.0) the prop is correctly documented and handled as aria-label, but in components such as ComboBox the prop is still ariaLabel.  We need to refactor each component that defines or consumes an ariaLabel prop to instead support aria-label (and deprecate ariaLabel).

2.explanation: Each of these component source files currently defines and consumes a prop named ariaLabel in its prop types or TypeScript interface. They are therefore inconsistent with HTML’s standard aria-label attribute and React’s recommendation to hyphen-case WAI-ARIA attributes. To fix the issue, these files need to deprecate the old ariaLabel prop, add support for ['aria-label'], and update internal usage to prefer the hyphenated attribute while maintaining backward compatibility.
2.bug_scenario: The accessibility prop naming is inconsistent across React components: some components accept the camel-cased ariaLabel prop (e.g. ComboBox’s story shows ariaLabel), while others (e.g. Modal) expect the hyphenated aria-label. Users and automated tools report missing labels or deprecation warnings when supplying aria-label to components that only recognize ariaLabel, and vice versa. To align with React’s recommendation and HTML WAI-ARIA attributes (which use hyphen-case), all components should support and prefer aria-label and deprecate ariaLabel.
